sources.title: Judicial Service of Ghana, Before Independence
sources.note: Constitutional chronology: 1874 colony, 1877 capital, separate administrations from 1902, Togoland mandate, and 1951 to 1954 reforms.

sources.title: UNESCO, Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions
sources.note: Outstanding Universal Value, fort architecture and changing roles in gold and slave trading. Earlier buildings are distinguished from the later colony.

sources.title: Christiansborg Archaeological Heritage Project, The Excavation
sources.note: Descendant community participation, excavated foundations, ceramics, beads and the tentative kitchen interpretation.

sources.title: Rachel Ama Asaa Engmann, Preliminary report on locally manufactured pottery from Christiansborg Castle, Ghana (2019)
sources.note: Pages 2 to 4 and 6: excavation context, dating limitations, soot, vessel forms and uncertain origins. Regional comparisons remain qualified.

sources.title: David Wilson, The Net That Catches the Most Fish: Fishing, Innovation, and Law in the Gold Coast Colony, c. 1898 to 1923 (2026)
sources.note: Fishing in Precolonial Ghana and Debating Fishing Nets: gendered work, competing origin accounts, ecological concerns and unequal returns.

sources.title: Ghana Cocoa Board, Cocoa Story
sources.note: Earlier introductions, Tetteh Quarshie’s 1879 return, Mampong cultivation and Aburi distribution from 1886.

sources.title: Ghana Cocoa Board, Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana: Pioneering Cocoa Sustainability and Innovation (2023)
sources.note: Institutional history: 1938 Central Cocoa Research Station at Akim Tafo and 1944 West African Cocoa Research Institute.

sources.title: Old Achimotan Association, History
sources.note: 1927 opening, subsequent branches, teacher training, vocational education, art, music and African dance.

sources.title: University of Ghana repository, Gold Coast Leader, April to July 1907
sources.note: Public catalogue metadata and abstract only. The embargoed issue scans were not consulted; no specific article content is claimed.

sources.title: Ghana Independence Act 1957, chapter 6
sources.note: Sections 1 and 5(2), printed pages 1 and 3. The appointed independence day was 6 March 1957.

identityAssociations.locator: 1877 transfer of capital to Accra; 1902 jurisdictional changes.
identityAssociations.scope: The imported 1900 Accra polygon exactly matches the earlier coastal Gold Coast outline, approximately 2.72 to 0.12 degrees west and 4.70 to 6.24 degrees north. It represents a coastal jurisdiction, not merely Accra city. The shared narrative preserves distinctions among the different territories.

identityAssociations.scope: The imported Ghana record begins in 1920 and covers a broader territory, approximately 3.20 degrees west to 1.16 degrees east and 4.70 to 11.13 degrees north. Its pre-independence label is clarified. The distinct modern ghana-1960 record is not associated with this colonial narrative.
